claims.statement_id: Sita disebut putri Bhumi dan anak angkat Raja Janaka dari Videha.

Sita, in her youth, chooses Rama, the prince of Ayodhya, as her husband in a svayamvara. After the svayamvara, she accompanies her husband to his kingdom but later chooses to accompany him along with her brother-in-law Lakshmana in his exile.

claims.statement_id: Ravana menculiknya dari hutan Dandaka dan menahannya di taman Ashoka Vatika di Lanka.
claims.quote: While in exile, the trio settles in the Dandaka forest from where she is abducted by Ravana, the Rakshasa king of Lanka. She is imprisoned in the garden of Ashoka Vatika in Lanka until she is rescued by Rama, who slays her captor.

claims.statement: In some versions, Sita demonstrates her chastity through the Agni Pariksha fire ordeal.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebagian versi, Sita membuktikan kesuciannya melalui ujian api Agni Pariksha.
claims.quote: After the war, in some versions of the epic, Rama asks Sita to undergo Agni Pariksha (an ordeal of fire), by which she proves her chastity, before she is accepted by Rama. Such an episode of trial makes Lakshmana angry at Rama, for the first time.

claims.statement: Other versions say Maya Sita replaces her during the abduction while the real Sita shelters in fire.
claims.statement_id: Versi lain menyebut Maya Sita menggantikannya saat diculik, sementara Sita asli berlindung dalam api.
claims.quote: In some other versions of the epic, Maya Sita, an illusion created by Agni, takes Sita's place and is abducted by Ravana and suffers his captivity, while the real Sita hides in the fire.

claims.statement: Some texts connect her previous birth with Vedavati.
claims.statement_id: Sejumlah teks menghubungkan kehidupan terdahulunya dengan Vedavati.
claims.quote: Some scriptures also mention her previous birth as Vedavati, a woman Ravana tries to molest.

claims.statement: In the continuation, Sita shelters in Valmiki's ashram and gives birth to twins Kusha and Lava.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kelanjutan kisah, Sita berlindung di asrama Valmiki dan melahirkan anak kembar Kusha dan Lava.
claims.quote: She takes shelter at Sage Valmiki's ashram. She gives birth to twin sons there: Kusha and Lava.

claims.statement: That ending recounts Sita's return to the earth, her mother.

claims.quote: Years later, Sita reunites her two sons with their father Rama and then returns to the womb of her mother, the earth, as a testimony to her ultimate purity.

claims.statement: The name Sita derives from a Sanskrit word meaning furrow.

claims.statement: Varuna is a Hindu god depicted as sovereign of the sky in early Vedic times.
claims.statement_id: Varuna adalah dewa Hindu yang digambarkan sebagai penguasa langit pada zaman Weda awal.
claims.quote: In the early Vedic era, Varuna is seen as the god-sovereign, ruling the sky and embodying divine authority.

claims.statement: He maintains truth and rta, cosmic and moral order.
claims.statement_id: Ia menjaga kebenaran dan rta, tatanan kosmis serta moral.
claims.quote: He maintains truth and ṛta, the cosmic and moral order, and was invoked as an omniscient ethical judge, with the stars symbolizing his watchful eyes or spies.

claims.statement: Varuna is frequently paired with Mitra.
claims.statement_id: Varuna sering dipasangkan dengan Mitra.
claims.quote: Frequently paired with Mitra, Varuna represents the magical and speculative aspects of sovereignty, overseeing the relationship between gods and humans.

claims.statement: In Itihasa and Purana traditions he becomes lord of oceans, rivers, streams, and lakes.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi Itihasa dan Purana ia menjadi penguasa lautan, sungai, aliran air, dan danau.
claims.quote: By the time of the Itihasa-Purana, Varuna had transformed into the lord of all waters, ruling over oceans, rivers, streams, and lakes.

claims.statement: He also serves as the dikpala guarding the west.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga berperan sebagai dikpala penjaga arah barat.
claims.quote: Varuna’s earlier supremacy diminished, and he was relegated to a lesser role as a dikpala, or guardian of the western direction.

claims.statement: His depictions include a youthful figure riding the creature Makara.
claims.statement_id: Penggambarannya mencakup sosok muda yang menunggang makhluk Makara.
claims.quote: He is depicted as a youthful man, mounted on Makara (crocodile-like creature) and holding a Pasha (noose, rope loop) and a pitcher in his hands.

claims.statement: He carries a pasha noose and pitcher.
claims.statement_id: Ia membawa jerat pasha dan kendi.
claims.quote: He is depicted as a youthful man, mounted on Makara (crocodile-like creature) and holding a Pasha (noose, rope loop) and a pitcher in his hands.

claims.statement: The Tolkappiyam calls him Kadalon, god of sea and rain.
claims.statement_id: Tolkappiyam menyebutnya Kadalon, dewa laut dan hujan.
claims.quote: Varuna is also mentioned in the Tamil grammar work Tolkāppiyam, as Kadalon ... the god of sea and rain, and is furthermore present as a deity in Jainism.

claims.statement: In Japanese Buddhism he is known as Suiten and belongs to the Twelve Devas.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Buddhisme Jepang ia dikenal sebagai Suiten dan termasuk Dua Belas Dewa.
claims.quote: In Japanese Buddhist myth, Varuna is known as Suiten ... and ranks among the Twelve Devas

claims.statement: A Hindu explanation connects his name with the root vr, meaning to encompass or bind.
claims.statement_id: Penjelasan Hindu mengaitkan namanya dengan akar vr yang berarti meliputi atau mengikat.
claims.quote: In Hindu tradition, the theonym Váruṇa (Devanagari: वरुण) is described as a derivation from the verbal root vṛ ("to surround, to cover" or "to restrain, bind") by means of a suffixal -uṇa-, for an interpretation of the name as  "he who covers or binds", in reference to the cosmological ocean or river encircling the world, but also in reference to the "binding" by universal law or Ṛta.

claims.statement: The Rigveda contains several Varuna hymns and depicts him as sky sovereign, guardian of rta, water deity, and wielder of maya.
claims.statement_id: Rigveda memuat sejumlah himne Varuna dan menggambarkannya sebagai raja langit, penjaga rta, penguasa air, serta pemilik maya.
claims.quote: Varuṇa is portrayed in four principal aspects: as a universal monarch and sovereign of the sky, the upholder of ṛta (cosmic order), a deity associated with water (āpah), and a wielder of māyā (cosmic illusion or creative power).

claims.statement: Rigveda 1.25 praises him for understanding the paths of birds, ships, and winds.
claims.statement_id: Rigveda 1.25 memujinya karena memahami lintasan burung, kapal, dan angin.
claims.quote: In Rigveda 1.25, Varuṇa is praised for his understanding of the paths of birds, the movement of ships and winds, and the secrets of time and space. Hymns characterize him as a sovereign deity, intimately acquainted with both the sacred and the profane.

claims.statement: Hymns depict him as punishing wrongdoing while showing mercy to the penitent.
claims.statement_id: Himne menggambarkannya menghukum pelanggaran tetapi mengasihi orang yang bertobat.
claims.quote: Varuṇa's foremost role is as the enforcer of ṛta, the cosmic and moral order that governs both the natural world and human conduct. Hymns such as Rigveda VII.11.1 and II.29.8 present him as a vigilant upholder of truth, who punishes transgressors while showing mercy to the penitent. Ethical instructions against killing, deceit, and gambling are linked with his domain.

claims.statement: The 1911 Britannica records the epithets Jalapati and Amburaja referring to lordship over water.
claims.statement_id: Britannica 1911 mencatat gelar Jalapati dan Amburaja yang merujuk penguasa air.
claims.quote:
Among Varuna's aliases are Jalapati, "Lord of Water," and 
Amburaja, " King of Water."

claims.statement_id: Ia memimpin pasukan deva melawan asura termasuk Tarakasura dan Surapadma.
claims.quote: He is described to have aged quickly from childhood, becoming a warrior, leading the army of the devas and credited with destroying asuras including Tarakasura and Surapadma.

claims.statement: Kartikeya means of the Krittikas, his nurses in the birth narrative.
claims.statement_id: Nama Kartikeya berarti milik para Krittika, pengasuhnya dalam cerita kelahiran.
claims.quote: Kartikeya means "of the Krittikas" in Sanskrit.

claims.statement: One account says Parvati merges six babies into six headed Kartikeya.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu cerita menyebut Parvati menyatukan enam bayi menjadi Kartikeya berkepala enam.
claims.quote: The epithet "Kartikeya" is linked to the circumstances surrounding the deity's birth. According to the Skanda Purana, six divine sparks emerged from Shiva, forming six separate baby boys. These boys were raised by handmaidens known as the Krittikas. Later, Parvati fused them into one, creating the six-headed Kartikeya. Kartikeya means "of the Krittikas" in Sanskrit.

claims.statement: The Vana Parva version of the Mahabharata describes him as the son of Agni and Svaha.
claims.statement_id: Versi Vana Parva Mahabharata menyebutnya putra Agni dan Svaha.
claims.quote: An alternate account of Kartikeya's parentage is narrated in the Vana Parva of the Mahabharata, where he is described as the son of Agni and Svaha.

claims.quote: Kartikeya- This statue, from the Later Gupta period, is made of red sandstone. ... He is a red god seated on a blue peacock, and his weapon, a spear, is engraved on the left of the sculpture.

regarded as the son of Agni and the Ganges.

claims.statement: Ravana is the rakshasa king of Lanka traditionally depicted with ten heads.
claims.statement_id: Ravana adalah raja rakshasa Lanka yang lazim digambarkan berkepala sepuluh.
claims.quote: He is traditionally depicted as a ten-headed rakshasa (demon) king of Lanka.

claims.statement: He is described as the son of Vishrava and Kaikasi.
claims.statement_id: Ia disebut putra Vishrava dan Kaikasi.
claims.quote: Ravana (Sanskrit: रावण, romanized: Rāvaṇa, lit. 'roaring') is the principal antagonist of the ancient Hindu epic Ramayana and its several other versions. He is traditionally depicted as a ten-headed rakshasa (demon) king of Lanka. In the Ramayana, Ravana is described as the eldest son of sage Vishrava and Kaikasi.

claims.statement: He abducts Sita and holds her in Ashoka Vatika.
claims.statement_id: Ia menculik Sita dan menahannya di Ashoka Vatika.
claims.quote: He abducted Rama's wife, Sita, and took her to his kingdom of Lanka, where he held her in the Ashoka Vatika.

claims.statement: Rama fights him with Sugriva and the vanara army's support and kills him.
claims.statement_id: Rama melawannya dengan dukungan Sugriva dan pasukan vanara lalu membunuhnya.
claims.quote: Rama, with the support of vanara King Sugriva and his army of vanaras, launched a rescue operation for Sita against Ravana in Lanka. Ravana was subsequently slain, and Rama rescued his beloved wife Sita.

claims.statement: His defeat is commemorated by burning Ravana effigies at Dussehra.
claims.statement_id: Kekalahannya diperingati dengan pembakaran patung Ravana pada Dussehra.
claims.quote: His epic defeat is celebrated yearly by burning a large effigy, depicting the ten-headed Ravana, during the Hindu festival of Dussehra.

claims.statement: Ravana is regarded as a devotee of Shiva.
claims.statement_id: Ravana dipandang sebagai pemuja Shiva.
claims.quote: Ravana was well-versed in the six shastras and the four Vedas, including the Shiva Tandava Stotra. Ravana is also considered to be an ardent devotee of Shiva. Images of Ravana are often seen associated with Shiva at temples. He also appears in the Buddhist Mahayana text Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra, in Buddhist Jatakas, as well as in Jain Ramayanas.

claims.statement: He also appears in the Lankavatara Sutra, Buddhist Jatakas, and Jain Ramayanas.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga hadir dalam Lankavatara Sutra, Jataka Buddha, dan Ramayana Jain.
claims.quote: Ravana was well-versed in the six shastras and the four Vedas, including the Shiva Tandava Stotra. Ravana is also considered to be an ardent devotee of Shiva. Images of Ravana are often seen associated with Shiva at temples. He also appears in the Buddhist Mahayana text Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra, in Buddhist Jatakas, as well as in Jain Ramayanas.

claims.statement: The name Ravana is explained as meaning roaring.
claims.statement_id: Nama Ravana diterangkan berarti mengaum.
claims.quote: The word Rāvaṇa (Sanskrit: रावण) means "Roaring" (active), the opposite of Vaiśravaṇa which means to "hear distinctly" (passive). Both Ravana and Vaiśravaṇa, who is commonly known as Kubera, are considered to be patronymics derived from "sons of Vishrava".

claims.statement: The epithet Dashanana means the one with ten heads.
claims.statement_id: Gelar Dashanana berarti yang berkepala sepuluh.
claims.quote: Dashānana was a title later taken on by Ravana, and it means "the one with ten (dasha) Heads (anana)". Further, roravana is Sanskrit for "loud roaring." In Abhinava Gupta's Krama Shaiva scripture, yāsām rāvanam is used as an expression to mean people who are truly aware of the materialism of their environment.

claims.statement: His other names include Lankapati and Lankeshwara.
claims.statement_id: Nama lainnya mencakup Lankapati dan Lankeshwara.
claims.quote: Ravana is also known by several other names including Dasis Ravana, Dasis Sakvithi Maha Ravana, Dashaanan, Ravula, Lankapati, Lankeshwara, Ravanasura and Ravanaeshwara.

claims.statement: Brahma grants him immunity against his creations except humans in the story.
claims.statement_id: Brahma memberinya anugerah kebal terhadap ciptaannya kecuali manusia dalam cerita.
claims.quote: Ravana and his two brothers, Kumbhakarna and Vibhishana, performed penance on Mount Gokarna for 10,000 years and won boons from Brahma. Ravana was blessed with a boon that would make him invincible to all the creations of Brahma, except for humans. He also received weapons, a chariot, as well as the ability to shapeshift from Brahma.

claims.statement: Brahma's gifts also include weapons, a chariot, and shapeshifting.
claims.statement_id: Anugerah Brahma juga mencakup senjata, kereta, dan kemampuan berganti wujud.
claims.quote: He also received weapons, a chariot, as well as the ability to shapeshift from Brahma.

claims.statement: Mandodari, Maya's daughter, is described as his chief queen.
claims.statement_id: Mandodari, putri Maya, disebut sebagai ratu utamanya.
claims.quote: According to Sundara Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, Ravana had over a thousand wives, with Mandodari, the daughter of the celestial architect Maya, being his chief queen. His sons were Meghanada, Atikaya, Akshayakumara, Narantaka, Devantaka and Trishira.

claims.statement: Mackenzie describes Rama as the slayer of Ravana who oppresses humans in the Ramayana.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menggambarkan Rama sebagai pembunuh Ravana yang menindas manusia dalam Ramayana.

Rama Chandra is the hero of the Ramáyana epic,
which is summarized in our closing chapters; he is the
human ideal of devotion, righteousness, and manliness,
the slayer of the demon Ravana, who oppressed and
persecuted mankind.

He is often identified with Dharmadeva, the personification of Dharma, though the two deities have different origins and myths.

claims.statement: Kala and Dharmaraja are other names of Yama.
claims.statement_id: Kala dan Dharmaraja merupakan nama lain Yama.
claims.quote: Yama (Sanskrit: यम, lit. 'twin'), also known as Kāla and Dharmarāja, is the Hindu god of death and justice, responsible for the dispensation of law and punishment of sinners in his abode, Naraka. He is often identified with Dharmadeva, the personification of Dharma, though the two deities have different origins and myths.

claims.statement: In Vedic tradition he is the first mortal to die and find the path to the abode of the dead.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi Weda ia adalah manusia pertama yang meninggal dan menemukan jalan ke tempat orang mati.
claims.quote: In Vedic tradition, Yama was considered the first mortal who died and espied the way to the celestial abodes; as a result, he became the ruler of the departed. His role, characteristics, and abode have been expounded in texts such as the Upanishads, the Ramayana, the Mahabharata, and the Puranas.

claims.statement: He is described as Yami's twin and the son of Surya and Sanjna.
claims.statement_id: Ia disebut saudara kembar Yami serta putra Surya dan Sanjna.
claims.quote: Yama is described as the twin of the goddess Yami, and the son of the god Surya (sun) (in earlier traditions Vivasvat) and Sanjna. He judges the souls of the dead and, depending on their deeds, assigns them to the realm of the Pitris (forefathers), Naraka (hell), or to be reborn on the earth.

claims.statement: He judges souls and assigns them according to their deeds to the ancestors' realm, Naraka, or rebirth.
claims.statement_id: Ia menilai jiwa dan menempatkannya menurut perbuatan ke alam leluhur, Naraka, atau kelahiran kembali.
claims.quote: Yama is described as the twin of the goddess Yami, and the son of the god Surya (sun) (in earlier traditions Vivasvat) and Sanjna. He judges the souls of the dead and, depending on their deeds, assigns them to the realm of the Pitris (forefathers), Naraka (hell), or to be reborn on the earth.

claims.statement: The form is divided equally into half male and half female.
claims.statement_id: Wujudnya dibagi sama rata menjadi setengah laki-laki dan setengah perempuan.
claims.quote: Ardhanarishvara (Sanskrit: अर्धनारीश्वर, romanized: Ardhanārīśvara, lit. 'the half-female Lord') is a form of the Hindu deity Shiva combined with his consort Parvati. Ardhanarishvara is depicted as half-male and half-female, equally split down the middle.

claims.statement: It symbolizes the union of masculine and feminine energies or Purusha and Prakriti.
claims.statement_id: Ia melambangkan penyatuan energi maskulin dan feminin atau Purusha dan Prakriti.
claims.quote: Ardhanarishvara represents the synthesis of masculine and feminine energies of the universe (Purusha and Prakriti) and illustrates how Shakti, the female principle of God, is inseparable from (or the same as, according to some interpretations) Shiva, the male principle of God, and vice versa. The union of these principles is exalted as the root and womb of all creation.

claims.statement: The right half is usually male Shiva.
claims.statement_id: Bagian kanan biasanya Shiva laki-laki.
claims.quote: The right half is usually the male Shiva, illustrating his traditional attributes.

claims.statement: Early depictions date to the Kushan period and develop in the Gupta era.
claims.statement_id: Penggambaran awal berasal dari periode Kushan dan berkembang pada era Gupta.
claims.quote: The earliest Ardhanarishvara images are dated to the Kushan period, starting from the first century CE. Its iconography evolved and was perfected in the Gupta era. The Puranas and various iconographic treatises write about the mythology and iconography of Ardhanarishvara.

claims.statement: The name Ardhanarishvara means the Lord who is half woman.
claims.statement_id: Nama Ardhanarisvara berarti Tuhan yang setengah perempuan.
claims.quote: The name Ardhanarishvara means "the Lord Who is half woman".

claims.statement: Cleveland's description of Ardhanarishvara shows the left side female and the right side male.
claims.statement_id: Deskripsi Cleveland tentang Ardhanarisvara memperlihatkan sisi kiri perempuan dan sisi kanan laki-laki.
claims.quote: his form in which the left side is female and the right side is male.

claims.statement: Daksha is a Hindu deity who in the Rigveda is an Aditya associated with priestly skills.
claims.statement_id: Daksha adalah dewa Hindu yang dalam Rigveda merupakan Aditya terkait keterampilan kependetaan.
claims.quote: is a Hindu god whose role underwent a significant transformation from Vedic to Itihasa-Puranic mythology. In the Rigveda, Daksha is an aditya and is associated with priestly skills.

claims.statement: In epics and Puranas he is Brahma's son and one of the Prajapatis, agents of creation.
claims.statement_id: Dalam wiracarita dan Purana ia adalah putra Brahma dan salah satu Prajapati, agen penciptaan.
claims.quote: In the epics and Puranic scriptures, he is a son of the creator-god Brahma and one of the Prajapati, the agents of creation, as well as a divine king-rishi.

claims.statement: His narrative describes a sacrifice deliberately excluding Sati and Shiva.
claims.statement_id: Kisahnya menyebut pengorbanan yang sengaja tidak mengundang Sati dan Shiva.
claims.quote: a resentful Daksha conducted a yajna (fire-sacrifice), and deliberately did not invite his youngest daughter Sati and her husband Shiva.

claims.statement: In the Linga Purana version Virabhadra beheads him and he later revives with a goat's head.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi Linga Purana, Virabhadra memenggalnya dan ia kemudian hidup kembali berkepala kambing.
claims.quote: In the Linga Purana, for insulting Shiva during this event, which caused Sati to self-immolate in fury, he was beheaded by Virabhadra, a fearsome form of Shiva. He was later resurrected with the head of a goat.

claims.statement: His iconography is a stocky man with a human face or goat's head.
claims.statement_id: Ikonografinya berupa laki-laki bertubuh kekar dengan wajah manusia atau kepala kambing.
claims.quote: His iconography depicts him as a man with a stocky body and a handsome face or the head of a goat.

claims.statement: In Mackenzie's retelling Shiva himself beheads Daksha and replaces his head with a goat's head.
claims.statement_id: Dalam retelling Mackenzie, Shiva sendiri memenggal Daksha dan mengganti kepalanya dengan kepala kambing.
claims.quote:
Daksha is the father of Sati, the peerless wife of
Shiva. It was on account of this rishi's quarrel with
her husband, who was not invited to a great feast, that
she flung herself upon the sacrificial fire. Shiva cut off
Daksha's head and replaced it with the head of a goat.

claims.statement_id: Tara adalah Buddha perempuan yang dipuja dalam Buddhisme Mahayana dan Vajrayana.
claims.quote: is an important female Buddha in Buddhism, especially revered in Vajrayana Buddhism and Mahayana Buddhism.

claims.statement: She is known as a saviouress hearing beings' cries and saving them from worldly and spiritual danger.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikenal sebagai penyelamat yang mendengar jeritan makhluk dan menyelamatkan dari bahaya duniawi dan rohani.
claims.quote: Tārā is also known as a saviouress who hears the cries of beings in saṃsāra and saves them from worldly and spiritual danger.

claims.statement: Green and White Tara are popular meditation deities or yidams in Tibetan Buddhism.
claims.statement_id: Tara Hijau dan Tara Putih merupakan dewa meditasi atau yidam yang populer dalam Buddhisme Tibet.
claims.quote: Both Green and White Tārā remain popular meditation deities or yidams in Tibetan Buddhism, and Tara is also revered in Newar Buddhism.

claims.statement: Green Tara emanates twenty one Taras with different attributes and activities.
claims.statement_id: Tara Hijau memancarkan 21 Tara dengan atribut dan kegiatan berbeda.
claims.quote: Green Tara emanates twenty-one Tārās, each with different attributes—colors, implements, and activities such as pacifying (śānti), increasing (pauṣṭika), enthralling (vaśīkaraṇa), and wrathful (abhicāra).

claims.statement: Tara's name is linked to a Sanskrit root for crossing, in the sense of causing to cross or rescuing.
claims.statement_id: Nama Tara dihubungkan dengan akar Sanskerta untuk menyeberang, dalam makna menyebabkan menyeberang atau menyelamatkan.
claims.quote: Tārā (Devanagari: तारा) is a feminine noun derived from the root √tṝ, "to cross". It is causative, and as such means "to cause to cross", i.e., "to rescue".

claims.statement: HAR states that Tara is practised in all schools of Tibetan Buddhism.
claims.statement_id: HAR menyatakan Tara dipraktikkan dalam semua aliran Buddhisme Tibet.
claims.quote: Practiced in all Schools of Tibetan Buddhism Tara is second in popularity only to Avalokiteshvara.

claims.statement: Bhairava is a deity worshipped in Shaiva and Vajrayana traditions.
claims.statement_id: Bhairava merupakan dewa yang dipuja dalam tradisi Shaiva dan Vajrayana.
claims.quote: is a Shaivite and Vajrayāna deity worshipped by Hindus and Buddhists.

claims.statement: In Shaivism he is a powerful manifestation or avatar of Shiva.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Shaivisme ia merupakan manifestasi atau avatar Shiva yang kuat.
claims.quote: In Shaivism, he is a powerful manifestation, or avatar, of Shiva.

claims.statement: He is called Dandapani for carrying a rod to punish sinners.
claims.statement_id: Ia disebut Dandapani karena membawa tongkat untuk menghukum pelaku dosa.
claims.quote: Bhairava is also called Daṇḍapāni ("he who holds the daṇḍa in his hand"), as he holds a rod or danda to punish sinners,

claims.statement: The epithet Shvashva means his vehicle is a dog.
claims.statement_id: Epitet Shvashva berarti ia memiliki kendaraan anjing.
claims.quote: Śvāśva, meaning, "he whose vehicle is a dog". In Vajrayana Buddhism, he is considered a fierce emanation

claims.statement: The Shiva Purana narrative recounts Bhairava beheading Brahma's fifth head to punish his lie.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Shiva Purana menuturkan Bhairava memenggal kepala kelima Brahma untuk menghukum kebohongannya.
claims.quote: Bhairava decapitated the fifth head of Brahma for uttering the falsehood.

claims.statement: In the continuation Brahma's skull leaves his hand when he arrives at Kashi.
claims.statement_id: Dalam lanjutan kisah, tengkorak Brahma terlepas dari tangannya setelah ia tiba di Kashi.
claims.quote: When Bhairava visited Kashi, the city of the liberated, Brahmahatya left him, and the skull of Brahma was released from his hand.

claims.statement: The Guimet Museum explains Bhairava as one of Shiva's fierce manifestations.
claims.statement_id: Museum Guimet menjelaskan Bhairava sebagai salah satu manifestasi ganas Shiva.
claims.quote: Bhairava, "le Terrible", l’une des manifestations farouches du dieu hindou Shiva.

claims.statement: Jagannath is a Hindu deity worshipped with his siblings Balabhadra and Subhadra.
claims.statement_id: Jagannath adalah dewa Hindu yang dipuja bersama saudaranya Balabhadra dan Subhadra.
claims.quote: Jagannath (Sanskrit: जगन्नाथ, Odia: ଜଗନ୍ନାଥ, romanized: Jagannātha, lit. 'Lord of the Universe', Odia pronunciation: [dʒɔɡɔnːat̪ʰɔ]; formerly English: Juggernaut) is a Hindu deity worshipped as part of a triad along with his brother, Balabhadra, and his sister, Subhadra.

claims.statement: Most Vaishnavas regard him as a regional form of Krishna or Vishnu.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian besar Waisnawa memandangnya sebagai bentuk regional Krishna atau Vishnu.
claims.quote: Jagannath, within Odia Hinduism, is the supreme god, Purushottama, and the Para Brahman. To most Vaishnava Hindus, Jagannath is a regional form of Krishna, sometimes as a form of Vishnu. To some Shaiva and Shakta Hindus, he is a symmetry-filled tantric form of Bhairava, a fierce manifestation of Shiva associated with annihilation.

claims.statement: His icon is decorated wood with large round eyes and no conspicuous hands or legs.
claims.statement_id: Ikonnya berupa kayu berhias dengan mata bulat besar dan tanpa tangan atau kaki yang menonjol.
claims.quote: The idol of Jagannath is a carved and decorated wooden stump with large round eyes and a symmetric face, and the idol has a conspicuous absence of hands or legs.

claims.statement: His wooden icon is replaced at regular intervals.
claims.statement_id: Ikon kayunya diganti secara berkala.
claims.quote: Unusually, the icon is made of wood and replaced with a new one at regular intervals.

claims.statement: The name Jagannath combines jagat and natha meaning Lord of the Universe.
claims.statement_id: Nama Jagannath menggabungkan jagat dan natha dalam arti penguasa alam semesta.
claims.quote: Jagannath is a Sanskrit word, compounded of jagat meaning "universe" and nātha meaning "Master" or "Lord". Thus, Jagannath means "lord of the universe".

claims.statement: Mackenzie recounts Jagannath's icon being carried in a great car drawn by worshippers once a year.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menuturkan ikon Jagannath dibawa dalam kereta besar yang ditarik pemuja sekali setahun.
claims.quote:
Once a
year the idol is bathed and afterwards taken forth in a
great car, which is dragged by pious worshippers.

claims.statement: Prithvi is the goddess personifying earth in Hinduism and a mother goddess in Vedic religion.
claims.statement_id: Prithvi adalah dewi personifikasi bumi dalam Hindu dan merupakan dewi ibu dalam agama Weda.
claims.quote: is the Sanskrit name for the Earth, as well as the name of the goddess-personification of it in Hinduism. The goddess Prithvi is an archetypal Mother Goddess, and one of the most important goddesses in the historical Vedic religion.

claims.statement: In the Vedas she is described as fertile, generous, and sustaining all beings.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Weda ia digambarkan subur, murah hati, dan memberi makan semua makhluk.
claims.quote: She is depicted as a stable, fertile, and benevolent presence in the Vedas. She is frequently addressed as a mother, and a nurturing, generous goddess who provides sustenance to all beings living on her vast, firm expanse. While the Rigveda predominantly associates her with Dyaus ('Father Sky'), the Atharvaveda and later texts portray her as an independent deity.

claims.statement: The Rigveda associates her with Dyaus, Father Sky; the Atharvaveda presents her as an independent goddess.
claims.statement_id: Rigveda mengaitkannya dengan Dyaus, Bapa Langit; Atharvaveda menampilkannya sebagai dewi mandiri.
claims.quote: She is depicted as a stable, fertile, and benevolent presence in the Vedas. She is frequently addressed as a mother, and a nurturing, generous goddess who provides sustenance to all beings living on her vast, firm expanse. While the Rigveda predominantly associates her with Dyaus ('Father Sky'), the Atharvaveda and later texts portray her as an independent deity.

claims.statement: In classical Hinduism her figure is supplanted by Bhumi, with Prithvi becoming an epithet of Bhumi.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Hindu klasik sosoknya digantikan Bhumi, dengan Prithvi menjadi salah satu epitet Bhumi.
claims.quote: In classical Hinduism, the figure of Prithvi is supplanted by the goddess Bhumi, while the term Prithvi serves as one of her epithets. She becomes significantly associated with Vishnu, one of the most important gods in later Hinduism, and two of his dashavatars—Varaha and Prithu.

claims.statement: The Prithu narrative recounts the earth goddess changing into a cow.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Prithu menuturkan dewi bumi berubah menjadi sapi.
claims.quote: Another connection is found between Prithvi and the mythological figure Prithu (Sanskrit: पृथु, Pṛthu), who chases the goddess Prthvi, shapeshifted as a cow. His name means 'far, wide, broad' and in later texts, the term Prithvi is treated as patronym for Earth derived from his name.

claims.statement: Rigveda 5.84 invokes Prithvi bearing the tool that rends hills and quickening earth.
claims.statement_id: Rigveda 5.84 menyeru Prithvi yang membawa alat pembelah bukit dan menghidupkan bumi.
claims.quote: THOU, of a truth, O Prthivi, bearest the tool that rends the hills: ... Thou rich in torrents, who with might quickenest earth, O Mighty One.

claims.statement: Shani is the divine personification of Saturn and a member of the Navagraha in Hinduism.
claims.statement_id: Sani adalah personifikasi ilahi planet Saturnus dan anggota Navagraha dalam Hindu.
claims.quote: is the divine personification of the planet Saturn in Hinduism, and is one of the nine heavenly objects (Navagraha) in Hindu astrology.

claims.statement: Depictions include a dark figure with sword or sceptre and buffalo or crow mount.
claims.statement_id: Penggambarannya mencakup tubuh gelap dengan pedang atau tongkat serta tunggangan kerbau atau gagak.
claims.quote: whose iconography consists of a figure with a dark complexion carrying a sword or danda (sceptre) and sitting on a buffalo or some times on a crow.

claims.statement: He is god of karma, time, and retribution for thoughts, speech, and deeds.
claims.statement_id: Ia merupakan dewa karma, waktu, dan balasan atas pikiran, ucapan, serta tindakan.
claims.quote: He is the god of karma, time and retribution, and delivers results depending upon one's thoughts, speech, and deeds.

claims.statement: In the narrative Shani's wife curses his gaze to cause destruction or hardship.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah, istri Sani mengutuk tatapannya agar menyebabkan kehancuran atau kesulitan.
claims.quote: Shani is married to the daughter of gandharva Chitraratha, who cursed him that anyone he gazed upon would face destruction or hardship.

claims.statement: Different texts depict his mount as crow, vulture, chariot, or other animals.
claims.statement_id: Berbagai teks berbeda menggambarkan tunggangannya sebagai gagak, burung nasar, kereta, atau hewan lain.
claims.quote: Shani is depicted wearing blue or black robes, having a dark complexion and riding a vulture or on an iron chariot drawn by eight horses. He holds in his hands a bow, an arrow, an axe and a trident. He is canonically represented riding on a large crow or vulture which follows him wherever he goes.

Puranas relates that the planet Saturn, being under a
curse, decapitated Ganesa simply by looking at him.

claims.statement: Together they are archetypal parents in the Rigveda.
claims.statement_id: Keduanya merupakan orang tua arketipal dalam Rigveda.
claims.quote: Dyaus (Vedic Sanskrit: द्यौस्, IAST: Dyáus) or Dyauspitr (Vedic Sanskrit: द्यौष्पितृ, IAST: Dyáuṣpitṛ́) is the Rigvedic sky deity. His consort is Prithvi, the earth goddess, and together they are the archetypal parents in the Rigveda.

claims.statement: The word dyaus without the word father refers to the daylight sky.
claims.statement_id: Kata dyaus tanpa kata ayah menunjuk langit siang.
claims.quote: The noun dyaús (when used without the pitṛ́ 'father') refers to the daylight sky, and occurs frequently in the Rigveda, as an entity. The sky in Vedic writing was described as rising in three tiers: avamá, madhyamá, and uttamá or tṛtī́ya.

claims.statement: Vedic scriptures mention Dyaus Pita with Prithvi Mata, Mother Earth.
claims.statement_id: Kitab Weda menyebut Dyaus Pita bersama Prithvi Mata, Ibu Bumi.
claims.quote: Dyáuṣ Pitṛ́ appears in hymns with Prithvi Mata, 'Mother Earth' in the ancient Vedic scriptures of Hinduism.

claims.statement: He is likened to a black stallion studded with pearls representing the night sky.
claims.statement_id: Ia diumpamakan sebagai kuda hitam bertabur mutiara yang menggambarkan langit malam.
claims.quote: Dyauṣ is also stated to be like a black stallion studded with pearls in a simile with the night sky.

claims.statement: Mackenzie connects Dyaus with the image of a ruddy bull whose bellowing is thunder.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menghubungkan Dyaus dengan gambaran banteng merah yang gemuruhnya adalah guntur.

claims.statement: Gandharvas are a class of celestial beings in Indian religions associated with music and dance.
claims.statement_id: Gandharva adalah golongan makhluk surgawi dalam agama India yang berhubungan dengan musik dan tari.
claims.quote: A gandharva (Sanskrit: गन्धर्व) is a member of a class of celestial beings in Indian religions, such as Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism, whose males are divine performers such as musicians and singers, and the females are divine dancers. In Hinduism, they are regarded to be the celestial demigods who serve as the musicians of the devas.

claims.statement: In Hinduism they are minor deities serving as divine musicians.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Hindu mereka merupakan dewa kecil yang menjadi musisi ilahi.
claims.quote: In Hinduism, the gandharvas (Sanskrit: गन्धर्व, romanized: gandharva) are a class of minor deities who serve as divine musicians in Hindu mythology.

claims.statement: In Vedic sources gandharva can also designate a single celestial being guarding Soma.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sumber Weda, gandharva juga dapat menunjuk satu makhluk surgawi yang menjaga Soma.
claims.quote: gandharva is presented as a celestial being (dwelling near the Sun / in the heavenly waters) which watches over the Soma

claims.statement: Gandharvas are generally called the husbands of apsaras.
claims.statement_id: Gandharva umumnya disebut sebagai suami para apsara.
claims.quote: They are generally the husbands of apsaras. They are described as handsome beings who wear fragrant attire and are passionate about women.

claims.statement: They usually live in Svarga and serve Indra's court.
claims.statement_id: Mereka biasanya hidup di Svarga dan melayani istana Indra.
claims.quote: Gandharvas usually live in Svarga and serve at Indra's court, though they also have their own realm, called the Gandharvaloka.

claims.statement: Mackenzie describes Gandharva music accompanying apsara dances.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menggambarkan musik Gandharva mengiringi tarian apsara.
claims.quote:
When they play on their divine instruments the fairy-like
Apsaras, who are all females, dance merrily.

claims.statement: Shukra is a mythological sage and presiding god of Venus in Hinduism.
claims.statement_id: Shukra merupakan resi mitologis dan dewa yang memimpin planet Venus dalam Hindu.
claims.quote: is a mythological sage as well as the presiding god of the planet Venus in Hinduism.

claims.statement: His other names are Ushanas and Kavya.
claims.statement_id: Nama lainnya Ushanas dan Kavya.
claims.quote: also known as Ushanas and Kavya, is a mythological sage as well as the presiding god of the planet Venus in Hinduism.

claims.statement: In the Rigveda he is the wise seer Kavya Ushanas and is not yet associated with Venus.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Rigveda ia merupakan resi bijak bernama Kavya Ushanas dan belum dikaitkan dengan Venus.
claims.quote: The figure later known as Shukra appears in the Vedic corpus primarily under the name Kavya Ushanas. ... Neither is there any attestation made to suggest that belonged to the Bhrigu clan nor his association with the planet Venus.

claims.statement: Later Sanskrit texts identify Ushanas, Kavya, Shukra, and Bhargava as names of the same figure.
claims.statement_id: Teks Sanskerta kemudian menyamakan Ushanas, Kavya, Shukra, dan Bhargava sebagai nama tokoh yang sama.
claims.quote: While the Vedic texts primarily refer to the figure as Ushanas Kavya, later Sanskrit literature introduces Shukra and Bhargava (lit. 'descendant of Bhrigu') serving as common epithets for the  sage named Ushanas. As a result, the names Ushanas, Kavya, Shukra and Bhargava came to be treated as referring to the same individual in the later tradition.

claims.statement: In later texts he is called Bhrigu's son or grandson and Kavyamata's son.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks kemudian ia disebut putra atau cucu Bhrigu dan putra Kavyamata.
claims.quote: Ushanas is mentioned as the son (or grandson in some texts) of the sage Bhrigu, one of the seven revered sages originating from the creator god Brahma. His mother is called Kavyamata (lit. 'mother of Kavya').

claims.statement: Later Puranas establish his role as priest and preceptor of the asuras.
claims.statement_id: Purana belakangan menetapkan perannya sebagai pendeta dan guru para asura.
claims.quote: By the time of the later Puranas, however, his role as the priest and preceptor of the asuras is firmly concretised.

claims.statement: He becomes associated with Venus and is most famous for possessing the Mrtasanjivani, a magical skill that can bring the dead back to life.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikaitkan dengan Venus dan paling terkenal karena memiliki Mrtasanjivani, keterampilan gaib yang dapat menghidupkan kembali orang mati.
claims.quote: He becomes associated with Venus and is most famous for possessing the Mṛtasañjīvanī—a magical skill that can bring the dead back to life.

claims.statement: In earlier texts he is portrayed as teacher of both the devas and the asuras, and in later texts he is established solely as the purohita of the asuras.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks-teks awal ia digambarkan sebagai guru para deva dan para asura, lalu dalam teks yang lebih akhir menjadi purohita para asura saja.
claims.quote: He is first portrayed as the teacher of both the devas (gods) and the asuras (antigods) in earlier texts, before becoming established solely as the purohita of the asuras in later texts.

claims.statement: The Mahabharata mentions that Ushanas divided himself into two halves, one the source of knowledge for the devas and the other for the asuras.
claims.statement_id: Mahabharata menyebut Ushanas membagi dirinya menjadi dua bagian: satu menjadi sumber pengetahuan bagi para deva dan satu lagi bagi para asura.
claims.quote: The Mahabharata mentions that Ushanas divided himself into two halves: one became the source of knowledge for the devas (gods), and the other for the asuras (demons).

claims.statement: In the Puranas, Shukra is blessed by Shiva with Sanjeevini Vidhya after performing tapas; it is knowledge of raising the dead back to life, which he used from time to time to restore life to the asuras.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Purana, Shukra diberkati Shiva dengan Sanjeevini Vidhya setelah bertapa; ilmu itu untuk menghidupkan kembali orang mati dan sesekali ia pakai untuk memulihkan nyawa para asura.
claims.quote: Shukra, in the Puranas, is blessed by Shiva with Sanjeevini Vidhya after performing tapas to propitiate Shiva. Sanjeevini Vidhya is the knowledge of raising the dead back to life, which he used from time to time to restore life to the asuras.

claims.statement: When Shukra, the asuras' guru, realised Vamana's true identity, he tried to stop the flow of water from the kamandalu by blocking the spout; Vamana pierced the spout with a stick and blinded Shukra.
claims.statement_id: Ketika Shukra, guru para asura, menyadari jati diri Vamana yang sebenarnya, ia mencoba menghalangi aliran air dari kamandalu dengan menutup cerat; Vamana menusuk cerat itu dengan tongkat dan membutakan Shukra.
claims.quote: When Shukra, the asuras' guru, had realised Vamana's true identity, he tried to prevent the flow of water from the kamandalu by blocking the spout, Vamana pierced the spout with a stick, blinded Shukra.

claims.statement: In the early medieval period (5th to 12th century CE), with the rise of anthropomorphic depictions of the Navagrahas, the planet Venus was personified as a youthful man with a white complexion, riding a white horse and holding a kamandalu (water pot).
claims.statement_id: Pada awal Abad Pertengahan (abad ke-5 sampai ke-12 M), seiring munculnya penggambaran Navagraha berwujud manusia, planet Venus dipersonifikasikan sebagai pemuda berkulit putih yang menunggang kuda putih dan memegang kamandalu (bejana air).
claims.quote: During the early medieval period (5th–12th century CE), with the rise of anthropomorphic depictions of the Navagrahas of Hindu astrology, the planet Venus was personified with a distinctive iconography: he is shown as youthful man with a white complexion, riding a white horse, and holding a kamandalu (water pot).

claims.statement: This iconographic form may or may not be identified with the sage Shukracharya.
claims.statement_id: Bentuk ikonografi ini mungkin atau mungkin tidak sama dengan resi Shukracharya.
claims.quote: This iconographic form may or may not be identified with the sage Shukracharya.

claims.statement: Some hymns credit Ushanas with providing or fashioning Indra's vajra (thunderbolt), though Tvashta is also referred to as its fashioner.
claims.statement_id: Beberapa himne mengaitkan Ushanas dengan penyediaan atau pembuatan vajra (petir) milik Indra, tetapi Tvashta juga disebut sebagai pembuat vajra itu.
claims.quote: Other hymns credit Ushanas with providing or fashioning Indra's vajra (thunderbolt), the weapon that later becomes Indra's defining attribute; though Tvashta is also referred to as Vajra's fashioner.

claims.statement: Ushanas is regarded as a renowned yogi endowed with extraordinary magical powers (siddhi); according to the Shanti Parva of the Mahabharata, he used them to enter Kubera, lord of the yakshas, depriving him of his wealth and freedom.
claims.statement_id: Ushanas dipandang sebagai tokoh terkemuka klannya, seorang yogi termasyhur yang memiliki kekuatan gaib luar biasa (siddhi); menurut Shanti Parva dalam Mahabharata, ia memakai kekuatan itu untuk memasuki Kubera, penguasa para yaksha, dan merampas kekayaan serta kebebasannya.
claims.quote: Ushanas is regarded as scion of his clan, noted as a renowned yogi endowed with extraordinary magical powers (siddhi). According to the Shanti Parva of the Mahabharata, he used these powers to enter Kubera, lord of the yakshas and ruler of Alaka, depriving him of both his wealth and freedom.

claims.statement: Shiva bent the trident with his hand, giving rise to his bow, Pinaka, then swallowed Ushanas.
claims.statement_id: Shiva membengkokkan trisula dengan tangannya sehingga lahir busurnya, Pinaka, lalu menelan Ushanas.
claims.quote: Shiva bent the trident with his hand, giving rise to his bow, Pinaka, then swallowed Ushanas.

claims.statement: In that account Ushanas came to be known as Shukra, a name signifying both "bright" and "semen".
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah itu, Ushanas kemudian dikenal sebagai Shukra, nama yang bermakna "terang" sekaligus "air mani".
claims.quote: Ushanas came to be known as Shukra, a name signifying both "bright" and "semen."

claims.statement: In the post-Vedic period, particularly in the epics (c. 400 BCE to 400 CE) and the Puranic texts (c. 300 CE to 1200 CE), Kavya Ushanas evolves into the seer-sage Ushanas, better known by the epithet Shukracharya.
claims.statement_id: Pada masa pasca-Weda, terutama dalam wiracarita (sekitar 400 SM – 400 M) dan teks Purana (sekitar 300 M – 1200 M), Kavya Ushanas berkembang menjadi resi Ushanas yang lebih dikenal dengan julukan Shukracharya.
claims.quote: In the post-Vedic period, particularly in the epics (c. 400 BCE – 400 CE) and the Puranic texts (c. 300 CE – 1200 CE), Kavya Ushanas evolves into the figure of seer-sage Ushanas, better known by the epithet Shukracharya.

claims.statement: In the Rigveda (c. 1500 BCE), Kavya Ushanas appears as a wise poet-priest associated with the gods, especially their king Indra, whom he helped defeat his enemies.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Rigveda (sekitar 1500 SM), Kavya Ushanas tampil sebagai pendeta-penyair bijak yang berhubungan dengan para dewa, terutama raja mereka, Indra, yang ia bantu mengalahkan musuh-musuhnya.
claims.quote: In the Rigveda (c. 1500 BCE), however, Kavya Ushanas appears as a wise poet-priest associated with the gods, especially their king Indra, whom he helped defeat his enemies.

claims.statement: Sukra (Venus) is described as a Brahmana born of Bhrigu and a native of Bhojakata.
claims.statement_id: Sukra (Venus) digambarkan sebagai seorang Brahmana kelahiran Bhrigu dan penduduk asli Bhojakata.
claims.quote: Sukra (Venus), likewise, is a Brahmana born of Bhrigu and a native of Bhojakata.

claims.statement: He is said to be seated in a golden chariot drawn by eight horses or in a silver chariot yoked to ten horses.
claims.statement_id: Ia disebut duduk di kereta emas yang ditarik delapan kuda atau di kereta perak yang ditarik sepuluh kuda.
claims.quote: he is seated in a golden chariot drawn by eight horses or in a silver chariot yoked to ten horses.

claims.statement: According to other authorities he has four arms in which are seen the staff, rosary, water-pot and the varada.
claims.statement_id: Menurut otoritas lain, ia berlengan empat, memegang tongkat, tasbih, bejana air, dan sikap varada.
claims.quote: According to other authorities he has four arms in which are seen the staff, rosary, water-pot and the varada.

claims.statement: The name Shukra (Sanskrit: शुक्र) literally means 'clear' or 'bright'.
claims.statement_id: Nama Shukra (Sanskerta: शुक्र) secara harfiah berarti 'jernih' atau 'terang'.
claims.quote: Sanskrit: शुक्र, lit. 'clear' or 'bright', IAST: Śukra

claims.statement: In Nepalese tradition Kumari is a living embodiment of Taleju Bhawani venerated through a Newar girl.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi Nepal, Kumari adalah perwujudan hidup Taleju Bhawani yang dipuja melalui seorang anak perempuan Newar.
claims.quote: also known as the Living Goddess, is a centuries‑old tradition in Nepal in which a prepubescent girl from the Newar community is venerated as a living embodiment of the goddess Taleju Bhawani (a form of Durga).

claims.statement: The practice involves Hindu and Buddhist devotees in the Kathmandu Valley.
claims.statement_id: Praktik ini melibatkan pemuja Hindu dan Buddha di Lembah Kathmandu.
claims.quote: The practice is central to the religious life of the Kathmandu Valley and draws devotees from both Hindu and Buddhist traditions.

claims.statement: Kumari derives from Sanskrit meaning virgin or young unmarried girl.
claims.statement_id: Kumari berasal dari Sanskerta dalam arti perawan atau gadis muda belum menikah.
claims.quote: The word Kumari is derived from Sanskrit, where it means "virgin" or "young unmarried girl". In the Newar language the term is also rendered as kumhaḥ (𑐎𑐸𑐩𑑂𑐴𑑅).

claims.statement: The foundation legend recounts Taleju disappearing after her secret meetings with the king are discovered.
claims.statement_id: Legenda pendirian menuturkan Taleju menghilang setelah pertemuan rahasianya dengan raja diketahui.
claims.quote: the goddess Taleju would visit the king nightly to play Tripasa (a dice game), on condition that he tell no one of their meetings. One night the king’s daughter followed him and discovered the goddess, who was angered and vanished.

claims.statement: In a dream Taleju asks the king to find a Shakya girl in whom she will manifest.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mimpi, Taleju meminta raja mencari gadis Shakya tempat ia akan mewujud.
claims.quote: Taleju later appeared in a dream, telling the king to search for a young Shakya girl in whom she would manifest.

claims.statement: The Nepal Tourism Board states that a Kumari candidate is selected from a Buddhist family of the Shakya clan.
claims.statement_id: Dewan Pariwisata Nepal menyatakan calon Kumari dipilih dari keluarga Buddhis klan Shakya.
claims.quote: A Kumari candidate is selected from a Buddhist family of Shakya clan.

claims.statement: In one Vedic creation myth Purusha is a cosmic being whose sacrifice by the gods creates life.
claims.statement_id: Dalam salah satu mitos penciptaan Weda, Purusha adalah makhluk kosmis yang pengorbanannya oleh para dewa menciptakan kehidupan.
claims.quote: In one of many creation myths of the early Vedas, Purusha was a cosmic being whose sacrifice by the gods created all life. In the Upanishads, the Purusha concept refers to the abstract essence of the Self, Spirit and the Universal Principle that is eternal, indestructible, without form, and all-pervasive.

claims.statement: The same term also means self, awareness, or universal principle in Indian philosophy.
claims.statement_id: Istilah yang sama memiliki makna lain sebagai diri, kesadaran, atau prinsip universal dalam filsafat India.
claims.quote: Purusha (Sanskrit: पुरुष, IAST: Puruṣa) is a concept in Vedic theology and Indian philosophy, variously referring the cosmic being or self, awareness, and universal principle.

claims.statement: Rigveda 10.90 describes Purusha with a thousand heads, eyes, and feet.
claims.statement_id: Rigveda 10.90 menggambarkan Purusha berkepala seribu, bermata seribu, dan berkaki seribu.
claims.quote: A THOUSAND heads hath Purusa, a thousand eyes, a thousand feet.

claims.statement: In the hymn Purusha is all that has been and all that is to be.
claims.statement_id: Himne tersebut menyebutnya segala yang telah ada dan yang akan ada.
claims.quote: This Purusa is all that yet hath been and all that is to be;

claims.statement: The gods prepare a sacrifice with Purusha as the offering.
claims.statement_id: Para dewa mempersiapkan pengorbanan dengan Purusha sebagai persembahan.
claims.quote: When Gods prepared the sacrifice with Purusa as their offering,

claims.statement: In the hymn the Moon is born from his mind and the Sun from his eye.
claims.statement_id: Dalam himne, Bulan lahir dari pikirannya dan Matahari dari matanya.
claims.quote: The Moon was gendered from his mind, and from his eye the Sun had birth;

claims.statement: Mackenzie describes Purusha as a giant who is the universe.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menggambarkan Purusha sebagai raksasa yang merupakan alam semesta.
claims.quote:
The Universe is the giant
Purusha (“man”); he is “all that hath been and shall
be”.

claims.statement: Shesha is a divine naga, king of serpents, and primordial creation being in Hinduism.
claims.statement_id: Shesha adalah naga ilahi, raja ular, dan makhluk primordial penciptaan dalam Hindu.
claims.quote: is a serpentine naga (serpent deity), and king of the serpents (Nagaraja), and a primordial being of creation in Hinduism.

claims.statement: Shesha is also known as Ananta or Ananta Shesha.
claims.statement_id: Shesha juga dikenal sebagai Ananta atau Ananta Shesha.
claims.quote: He is also known as Ananta ... or Ananta Shesha

claims.statement: Vishnu as Narayana is commonly depicted resting on Shesha with Lakshmi.
claims.statement_id: Vishnu dalam bentuk Narayana lazim digambarkan beristirahat di atas Shesha bersama Lakshmi.
claims.quote: Vishnu, in his Narayana form, is traditionally depicted as resting on Shesha alongside his consort Lakshmi.

claims.statement: In tradition he incarnates as Lakshmana and Balarama.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi, ia berinkarnasi sebagai Lakshmana dan Balarama.
claims.quote: Shesha is traditionally believed to have incarnated on Earth as Lakshmana, the younger brother of Vishnu's incarnation Rama during the Treta Yuga, and as Balarama, the elder brother of Vishnu's incarnation Krishna during the Dvapara Yuga.

claims.statement: His iconography can have five, seven, or ten hoods, while classical texts often describe a thousand heads.
claims.statement_id: Ikonografinya dapat berkepala lima, tujuh, atau sepuluh, sementara teks klasik sering menyebut seribu kepala.
claims.quote: Shesha is generally depicted with a large coiled form floating through cosmic space or upon the Ocean of Milk, forming the bed upon which Vishnu rests. In iconography, he is depicted with multiple hoods—often five, seven or ten—though classical texts frequently describe him with one thousand crowned heads.

claims.statement: Mackenzie also calls Balarama an incarnation of the world serpent Shesha.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie juga menyebut Balarama sebagai inkarnasi ular dunia Shesha.
claims.quote:
Balarama is an incarnation of the world serpent
Shesha.

claims.statement: Adityas are a class of Hindu deities generally regarded as solar gods and Aditi's offspring.
claims.statement_id: Aditya adalah kelompok dewa Hindu yang umumnya dianggap dewa matahari dan keturunan Aditi.
claims.quote: refers to a class of Hindu deities. They are usually presented as solar deities, and the offspring of the Goddess Aditi.

claims.statement: Their number is six to eight in the Rigveda and increases to twelve in the Brahmanas.
claims.statement_id: Jumlah mereka enam sampai delapan dalam Rigveda dan meningkat menjadi dua belas dalam Brahmana.
claims.quote: They are first attested in the Rig Veda, where they are 6–8 in number, all male. The number increases to 12 in the Brahmanas.

claims.statement: In the Mahabharata and Puranas Kashyapa is called their father.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Mahabharata dan Purana, Kashyapa disebut sebagai ayah mereka.
claims.quote: The  epic Mahabharata and the Puranic scriptures mention the sage Kashyapa  as their father,

claims.statement: The Rigveda describes the Adityas as bright, pure, and free from falsehood.
claims.statement_id: Rigveda menggambarkan Aditya terang, murni, dan bebas dari kepalsuan.
claims.quote: The Aditya have been described in the Rig Veda as bright and pure as streams of water, free from all guile and falsehood, blameless, perfect.

claims.statement: The twelve Adityas are regarded as representing twelve months and aspects of the Sun.
claims.statement_id: Dua belas Aditya dipandang mewakili dua belas bulan dan aspek Matahari.
claims.quote: In present-day usage in Sanskrit, the term Aditya has been made singular in contrast to Vedic Adityas, and is being used synonymously with Surya, the Sun. The twelve Adityas are believed to represent the twelve months in the calendar and the twelve aspects of Sun. Since they are twelve in number, they are referred as DvadashAdityas.

claims.statement: Mackenzie discusses Mitra, Varuna, and Aryaman as members of the Aditya group.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie membahas Mitra, Varuna, dan Aryaman sebagai anggota kelompok dewa Aditya.
claims.quote:
Mitra as Mithra with Varuna, and a third vague god,
Aryaman, belong to an early group of equal deities called
the Adityas, or “Celestial deities”.

claims.statement: Makara is a legendary sea creature in Hindu mythology; in Hindu astrology, Makara is equivalent to the Zodiac sign Capricorn.
claims.statement_id: Makara adalah makhluk laut legendaris dalam mitologi Hindu; dalam astrologi Hindu, Makara setara dengan zodiak Capricorn.
claims.quote: is a legendary sea-creature in Hindu mythology. In Hindu astrology, Makara is equivalent to the Zodiac sign Capricorn.

claims.statement: It serves as the mount of Ganga, Narmada, and Varuna.
claims.statement_id: Ia menjadi tunggangan Ganga, Narmada, dan Varuna.
claims.quote: Makara appears as the vahana (vehicle) of the river goddess Ganga, Narmada, and of the god of the ocean, Varuna.

claims.statement: Makaras are regarded as guardians of gateways and thresholds of temples and throne rooms.
claims.statement_id: Makara dianggap penjaga gerbang dan ambang kuil serta ruang takhta.
claims.quote: Makara are considered guardians of gateways and thresholds, protecting throne rooms as well as entryways to temples;

claims.statement: The Sanskrit word makara means sea animal or crocodile.
claims.statement_id: Kata Sanskerta makara berarti hewan laut atau buaya.
claims.quote: Makara is a Sanskrit word which means "sea-animal, crocodile".

claims.statement: Its common form combines a terrestrial animal's front with an aquatic animal's rear.
claims.statement_id: Bentuk umumnya menggabungkan bagian depan hewan darat dengan bagian belakang hewan air.
claims.quote: It is generally depicted as half terrestrial animal in the frontal part (stag, deer, or elephant) and half aquatic animal in the hind part (usually of a fish, a dolphin, or a snake, though sometimes a peacock or even a floral tail is depicted).

claims.statement: In Sinhalese artwork a makara combines parts of several animals such as elephant trunk and crocodile jaws.
claims.statement_id: Dalam karya Sinhala, makara menggabungkan bagian beberapa hewan, seperti belalai gajah dan rahang buaya.
claims.quote: In Sinhalese ancient artwork Makara is made up of body parts of six or seven animals such as the trunk of the elephant, jaws of the crocodile, ears of the mouse or ape, extruding teeth of wild swine, the tail plume of the peacock and feet of the lion.

claims.statement: Makara is also the insignia of the love god Kamadeva, who is also known as Makaradhvaja, "one whose flag depicts a makara".
claims.statement_id: Makara juga menjadi lambang dewa cinta Kamadeva, yang juga dikenal sebagai Makaradhvaja, "dia yang benderanya menggambarkan makara".
claims.quote: Makara is also the insignia of the love god Kamadeva, who has no dedicated temples and is also known as Makaradhvaja, "one whose flag depicts a makara".

claims.statement: Makara is the most commonly recurring creature in Hindu and Buddhist temple iconography, and also frequently appears as a gargoyle or as a spout attached to a natural spring.
claims.statement_id: Makara adalah makhluk yang paling sering muncul dalam ikonografi kuil Hindu dan Buddha, dan juga kerap tampil sebagai gargoyle atau pancuran yang menempel pada mata air alami.
claims.quote: it is the most commonly recurring creature in Hindu and Buddhist temple iconography, and also frequently appears as a gargoyle or as a spout attached to a natural spring.

claims.statement: In Vedic times Varuna (the Vedic water god) became the god of the seas and rode on makara, which was called "the water monster vehicle".
claims.statement_id: Pada masa Weda, Varuna (dewa air Weda) menjadi dewa lautan dan menunggang makara, yang disebut "kendaraan monster air".
claims.quote: During Vedic times when Indra was the god of heaven, Varuna (the Vedic water god) became the God of the seas and rode on makara, which was called "the water monster vehicle".

claims.statement: Makara-shaped earrings called Makarakundalas are sometimes worn by Hindu deities, for example Shiva, Vishnu, Surya, and Chandi.
claims.statement_id: Anting berbentuk makara yang disebut Makarakundala kadang dikenakan dewa-dewi Hindu, misalnya Shiva, Vishnu, Surya, dan Chandi.
claims.quote: Makara-shaped earrings called Makarakundalas are sometimes worn by Hindu deities, for example Shiva, Vishnu, Surya, and Chandi.

claims.statement: Makara is a mythical sea creature believed to be the mount of the deities Ganga, Narmada and Varuna.
claims.statement_id: Makara adalah makhluk laut mitos yang dipercaya menjadi tunggangan dewa-dewi Ganga, Narmada, dan Varuna.
claims.quote: it is a mythical sea creature that is believed to be the mount of the deities Ganga, Narmada and Varuna.

claims.statement: Makara is often depicted with a terrestrial front half (elephant, antelope etc.) and an aquatic back half (fish, crocodile etc.).
claims.statement_id: Makara sering digambarkan dengan separuh depan hewan darat (gajah, antelop, dan sebagainya) dan separuh belakang hewan air (ikan, buaya, dan sebagainya).
claims.quote: It is often depicted with a terrestrial (elephant, antelope etc.) front half and an aquatic (fish, crocodile etc.) back half.

claims.statement: The caption describes a sandstone lintel from a temple at Beshnagar (c. 500 CE) on which the goddess Ganga, the Hindu personification of the River Ganges, stands on a makara (a mix of crocodile and elephant) which symbolises the life-giving nature of water.
claims.statement_id: Keterangan gambar ini menyebut sebuah lintel batu pasir dari sebuah kuil di Beshnagar (sekitar 500 M): dewi Ganga, personifikasi Sungai Gangga dalam Hindu, berdiri di atas makara (campuran buaya dan gajah) yang melambangkan sifat air yang memberi kehidupan.
claims.quote: Ganga, the Hindu personification of the River Ganges. A sandstone lintel from a temple at Beshnagar, c. 500 CE. The goddess stands on a makara (a mix of crocodile and elephant) which symbolises the life-giving nature of water.

claims.statement: From the 2nd century BCE, the makara appears to have been the symbol of Pradyumna, son of Vasudeva Krishna.
claims.statement_id: Sejak abad ke-2 SM, makara tampaknya menjadi lambang Pradyumna, putra Vasudeva Krishna.
claims.quote: From the 2nd century BCE, the Makara appears to have been the symbol of Pradyumna, son of Vāsudeva Krishna.

claims.statement: The leading Hindu temple architect and builder Ganapati Sthapati describes the makara as a mythical animal with the body of a fish, trunk of an elephant, feet of a lion, eyes of a monkey, ears of a pig, and the tail of a peacock.
claims.statement_id: Arsitek dan pembangun kuil Hindu terkemuka, Ganapati Sthapati, menggambarkan makara sebagai hewan mitos bertubuh ikan, berbelalai gajah, berkaki singa, bermata kera, bertelinga babi, dan berekor merak.
claims.quote: The leading Hindu temple architect and builder Ganapati Sthapati describes Makara as a mythical animal with the body of a fish, trunk of an elephant, feet of a lion, eyes of a monkey, ears of a pig, and the tail of a peacock.

claims.statement: Several German scientists argued that makara is based on the dugong instead, based on a reading of the Jain text Suryaprajnapti; the South Asian river dolphin may also have contributed to the image of the makara.
claims.statement_id: Beberapa ilmuwan Jerman berpendapat makara justru didasarkan pada dugong, berdasarkan pembacaan teks Jain Suryaprajnapti; lumba-lumba sungai Asia Selatan mungkin juga menyumbang pada citra makara.
claims.quote: Several German scientists argued that makara is based on the dugong instead, based on reading of Jain text of Sūryaprajñapti. The South Asian river dolphin may also have contributed to the image of the makara.

claims.statement: Though the makara may take many different forms in Hindu culture, in the modern world its form is always related to the marsh crocodile or water monitor.
claims.statement_id: Meskipun makara dapat berwujud macam-macam dalam budaya Hindu, di dunia modern wujudnya selalu dikaitkan dengan buaya rawa atau biawak air.
claims.quote: Though Makara may take many different forms throughout Hindu culture, in the modern world, its form is always related to the marsh crocodile or water monitor.

issues.message: Diusulkan dilewati: Identitas utama pada artikel adalah personifikasi nasional India dan simbol nasionalisme yang lahir dari sastra serta seni abad ke-19, kemudian dipopulerkan melalui novel Anandamath (1882). Ini personifikasi politik modern, bukan tokoh mitologi atau cerita rakyat tradisional dalam cakupan entri baru. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharat_Mata).
